const values = [1, 2, 3];
const result: number = values[5] ?? "fallback";
console.log(result);
const optional: {x?: string} = {};
console.log(optional.x ?? 0);
if (0x0) console.log("zero");
if (1.0) console.log("decimal one");
if (0b1) console.log("binary one");
if (0o1) console.log("octal one");
function constrainedNumber<T extends number>(n: T) { const value: number = n ?? "bad"; return value; }
function constrainedChain<U extends number, T extends U>(n: T): T { return n ?? "bad"; }
function constrainedUnion<T extends string | number>(n: T): T { return n ?? false; }
function constrainedObject<T extends {}>(n: T): T { return n ?? "bad"; }
function nullableNumber<T extends number | null>(n: T): number { return n ?? 0; }
function optionalNumber<T extends number | undefined>(n: T): number { return n ?? 0; }
console.log(constrainedNumber(1), constrainedChain(2), constrainedUnion("a"), constrainedObject({x: 1}));
console.log(nullableNumber(null), nullableNumber(3), optionalNumber(undefined), optionalNumber(4));
type NullishNumber<S> = S extends string ? number | null : number;
function conditionalNumber<S, T extends NullishNumber<S>>(n: T): number { return n ?? 0; }
function indexedNumber<S extends {x: number | null}, T extends S["x"]>(n: T): number { return n ?? 0; }
console.log(conditionalNumber<string, number | null>(null), indexedNumber<{x: number | null}, number | null>(null));
